method: Frozen 123-test table from docs/realtime-tests.md; exact PASS records from the two linked ARM64 logs; static tracing of each test, helper and code/child timer. No assertions or timers changed.
timing_boundary: Per-test nextest PASS durations, excluding queue, compilation and runner setup; use the maximum per identity across the two runs. Their sum is not one measured suite wall time.

current_local_enumeration.command: cargo nextest list --locked --release --build-jobs 4 -p lamp-voice -p lamp-voice-eval -p lamp-memory -p lamp-health -p lamp-records -p lamp-actions --profile realtime --message-format json

wait_kinds.test_sleep: Test-owned pacing, elapsed observation windows or polling; a guard never implies the full duration is consumed.
wait_kinds.code_deadline: Elapsed-time scheduling or bounded I/O in the exercised path; see each wait role/detail to distinguish elapsed conditions, event waits and failure guards.
wait_kinds.child_real_time: A real OS child must advance its own wall/monotonic timer; changing only a parent clock cannot advance it.

w170.detail: Observe real memory child readiness. Polling exits as soon as ready; 8 s is not a mandatory delay.

w171.detail: Bound each real request/reply, retaining protocol and storage assertions. Successful local replies do not normally consume the timeout.

w172.timing: 8 s predicate guard; bus receives in slices of at most 250 ms.
w172.detail: Wait for a diagnostic matching the asserted state and answer count. Returns on the matching report; not a fixed 8 s or 250 ms delay.

w173.timing: REPORT_EVERY = 1 s; Instant-based deadline and thread::park_timeout; wakeups recheck the same deadline.
w173.detail: The spawned lamp-memory binary owns an independent reporter thread, periodically reads counts and publishes while the request owner may block on accept. A report can be immediate if the store is ready before the first snapshot; later matching reports require real reporter cycles. The OPENING phase does not publish.

w174.timing: 5 ms polling, doubling to 50 ms; 8 s failure guard.
w174.detail: Wait for an actual delivery-failed/recovered transition in child stderr. This observes the reporter cycle; polling alone is not the main delay.

w175.timing: REPORT_EVERY * 3 = 3 s; sleeps at most 200 ms while continuing real status requests.
w175.detail: Hold a previously functioning bus broken across three further report periods and prove no false recovery or repeated failure log. This negative interval is mandatory in the current test; reporter retries are production behavior, not test retries.

w176.timing: Once per process: warm-up streams 100 blocks at 10 ms, nominally about 1 s, with up to three catch_unwind attempts.
w176.detail: Warm the real DSP before the counted session so emulation/cold initialization does not trip real 40 ms guards. Nextest runs each test in its own process, so each measured invocation normally pays one successful warm-up. Existing retry-like warm-up is inherited, not proposed.

w177.timing: Handshake polls every 500 us; failure bound 5 s.
w177.detail: Drive real worker Ready/Prepared and reference priming/start handshake. Exits on handshake completion; no mandatory 5 s wait.

w178.timing: Settle polls every 500 us; guard 500 ms.
w178.detail: Wait until scripted device data is read and all frames except the asserted hold are delivered. Used by warm-up and normal hold/no-hold/mute sessions. The busy-start main session omits settle; do not count 500 ms as a fixed delay.

w179.timing: Stop polls every 500 us with a 2 s guard; after join, 50 iterations each sleep 1 ms.
w179.detail: Receive stopped, join the worker successfully, then prove no frame arrives after stop. The final nominal 50 ms is mandatory in both successful warm-up and main session; the 2 s guard is not.

w180.timing: Parent renews authority every 40 ms; real worker ticks every 2 ms and uses a 100_000 us priming barrier.
w180.detail: Keep authority live and process control, reference and capture with production timing guards. These run in a thread in the test process. They must progress alongside scripted audio rather than being bypassed by dumping all samples at once.

w181.timing: Maximum capture read 10_000 us; at most four capture blocks unread (40 ms); reference maximum age 40_000 us; reference-channel handshake deadline 3_000_000 us; envelope-specific ages are checked against monotonic_us.
w181.detail: Reject slow/stale capture or reference data and stale transport/control ownership. ScriptedCapture’s optional read stall is not configured in any of these four tests; its conditional sleep is not an executed wait here.

w182.timing: Main session 400 blocks at TICK = 10 ms; tick 0 is immediate, last due at 3990 ms; wait loop sleeps 300 us.
w182.detail: Pace render reference and microphone samples at real audio speed so DSP, hold and age checks see realistic ordering. The audio fixture duration is substantive coverage; the same blocks can be driven in virtual time only with synchronized worker and transport clocks.

w183.timing: Main session 400 blocks at TICK = 10 ms; tick 0 is immediate, last due at 3990 ms; wait loop sleeps 300 us.
w183.detail: Pace render reference and microphone samples at real audio speed so DSP, hold and age checks see realistic ordering. The audio fixture duration is substantive coverage; the same blocks can be driven in virtual time only with synchronized worker and transport clocks.

w184.timing: 10 ms startup polling, WAIT = 30 s failure bound.
w184.detail: Observe the actual lamp-health child subscribing/starting. Not a required 30 s delay.

w185.timing: First/board receives bounded by 30 s; second health polled with 100 ms receive timeouts under a 30 s guard.
w185.detail: Continuously inspect notices while waiting for the second health message. The 5 s report gap, not the 30 s guard, dominates successful execution.

w186.timing: Default health_every = 5 s, board_every = 5 s, report_every = 1 s, tick = 100 ms; Instant deadlines and bus socket waits.
w186.detail: Run the real service across the interval between first and second periodic healths, while retaining board and diagnostic activity. Header at_us also derives from real elapsed time; preserve the asserted gap rather than shortening the production constants.

w187.timing: Bus default lease = 3 s; publisher liveness uses Instant refresh and filesystem mtimes compared against SystemTime.
w187.detail: Keep both topics alive across a 5 s publication gap, proving subscribers never report the source gone or late. A virtual service clock alone leaves this essential lease proof on the wrong clock.

w188.timing: 4 s guard per matching diagnostic; subscriber receives with the remaining time.
w188.detail: Await each observed configuration/receipt transition while verifying the real child is still alive. Six observed statuses; success returns early, so no fixed 4 s per stage.

w189.timing: Reporting loop immediately publishes, then sleeps 1 s minus work time; CLI --seconds 30 caps lifetime.
w189.detail: Reload switch/policy and receipt files once per real reporting iteration. The 30 s cap is an independent failure guard; the test kills/reaps the child on completion. Five subsequent 1 s intervals explain the 5.0 s baseline.

w190.timing: Two backends; each observes 2.2 s with 100 ms sleeps (4.4 s total nominal windows).
w190.detail: Prove LAMP_BUS_ROOT alone does not opt into reporting or create bus data while the server stays alive. Mandatory negative observation in the current test, spanning two nominal reporter periods per backend.

w191.timing: 10 ms polling; each until call has a 5 s guard.
w191.detail: Observe readiness, five light actions appearing, then withdrawal after owner departure. Polling exits on predicates; the 5 s bounds are not fixed sleeps.

w192.timing: Synthetic owner publishes every 20 ms; messages expire after 600 ms.
w192.detail: Read wanted state and confirm actual bus changes; eventually stop refreshing the light state. The source comment says once a second, but executed code sleeps 20 ms; code governs.

w193.timing: LOOK_AGAIN = 2 s; IDLE = 50 ms, using Instant.
w193.detail: The real serve loop in a test-created thread refreshes its offered-action catalog. The appearance and withdrawal refresh cycles explain most of the 4.1 s baseline; exact additive wall time is not inferred.

w194.timing: Confirmation at most 600 ms, polling every 15 ms.
w194.detail: Successful on/colour/dimmer calls wait for the synthetic owner to show the requested state. Normally released by the next 20 ms owner publication; the timeout should not be reached.

w195.timing: SystemTime wall expiry; test header sets 600 ms, overriding BusLight default 3000 ms.
w195.detail: Withdraw an owner whose last published state is stale. Must control both published wall timestamp and the expiry comparison, not only serve Instant.

w196.timing: Client read timeout 3 s; server caller read/write timeout 1 s.
w196.detail: Bound real Unix-socket calls. Not expected fixed delays; owner/server joins after stop are completion waits, not timed fixtures.

w197.timing: Main session 100 blocks at TICK = 10 ms; tick 0 is immediate, last due at 990 ms; wait loop sleeps 300 us.
w197.detail: Pace render reference and microphone samples at real audio speed so DSP, hold and age checks see realistic ordering. The audio fixture duration is substantive coverage; the same blocks can be driven in virtual time only with synchronized worker and transport clocks.

w198.timing: Main session 50 blocks at TICK = 10 ms; tick 0 is immediate, last due at 490 ms; wait loop sleeps 300 us.

w199.timing: Exactly 3 injected BUSY open errors; production retry allowance < 3 s from first busy answer; worker tick 2 ms.
w199.detail: Permit a briefly occupied microphone to open and finish the existing readiness handshake. No configured wall sleep in ScriptedCapture; success occurs after the injected failures are consumed, normally after a few worker ticks.

w200.timing: 5 ms polling, doubling to 50 ms; 8 s exit guard.
w200.detail: Observe each corrupt-store child exiting with status 1. No required 8 s delay.

w201.detail: After child exit, inspect any delivered final diagnostics; absence is explicitly allowed. These roughly 0.5 s total windows dominate the measured 0.5 s. They are receive timeouts, not thread::sleep calls.

w202.timing: Reporter starts before store open; failure finish unparks it and waits at most SHUTDOWN_WAIT = 100 ms.
w202.detail: Bound best-effort failed-start publication and shutdown. Completion may happen sooner. The normal 1 s report cadence is not a required delay on this failure path.
